headline: Haaland's brace puts Norway ahead 2-1 against Iraq at halftime
summary: Erling Haaland scored twice to give Norway the lead in a World Cup Group I match held at New York New Jersey Stadium.
details: Norway leads Iraq 2-1 at the end of the first half of their World Cup Group I match. The game is taking place at the New York New Jersey Stadium.
Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 29th minute, converting a cross from David Møller.
Iraq fought back quickly, with Aymen Hussein scoring a header in the 39th minute following a cross from Amir Al-Amari to level the score.
Haaland's second goal ensured Norway maintained a lead going into the break.
caption:
Erling Haaland strikes twice! Norway leads Iraq 2-1 at the half.

Norway leads Iraq 2-1 at the end of the first half of their World Cup Group I match. The game is taking place at the New York New Jersey Stadium.

headline_marked: Brazil's [[Neymar returns to training]] at World Cup after calf injury
headline: Brazil's Neymar returns to training at World Cup after calf injury
summary: The all-time record scorer for Brazil took a key step in his recovery process at the team's training base in New Jersey.
details: Brazil forward Neymar trained at the World Cup for the first time on Tuesday, signalling that he may be nearing a return to the pitch.
The 34-year-old has been undergoing treatment for a right calf injury diagnosed in late May and was seen running at the team's training base in New Jersey.
Despite the progress, Neymar has yet to return to full training and missed Brazil's opening 1-1 draw against Morocco on Saturday.
The star has been a staple of Brazil's last three World Cup campaigns, though his inclusion this time was surprising as injuries kept him out of national team play since 2023.
Fitness issues have also limited his club appearances this year, with Neymar featuring in only half of his team's games across the Brazilian league, cup, and Copa Sudamericana.
Brazil is scheduled to play Haiti in Philadelphia this Friday, followed by a final Group C match against Scotland in Miami on June 24.
caption:
Neymar is back on the grass! 🇧🇷 The Brazilian star has officially returned to training at the World Cup.

Brazil forward Neymar trained at the World Cup for the first time on Tuesday, signalling that he may be nearing a return to the pitch.

The 34-year-old has been undergoing treatment for a right calf injury diagnosed in late May and was seen running at the team's training base in New Jersey.

Despite the progress, Neymar has yet to return to full training and missed Brazil's opening 1-1 draw against Morocco on Saturday.

The star has been a staple of Brazil's last three World Cup campaigns, though his inclusion this time was surprising as injuries kept him out of national team play since 2023.

Fitness issues have also limited his club appearances this year, with Neymar featuring in only half of his team's games across the Brazilian league, cup, and Copa Sudamericana.

Brazil is scheduled to play Haiti in Philadelphia this Friday, followed by a final Group C match against Scotland in Miami on June 24.
